title: Hostile coverage: authority transport boundaries
description:
Objective: hostile before/after/race coverage for the TRANSPORT axis of the declared-boundary roster. SPIDR child of the Security fault matrix (task-05ce9b8f982f448a9cdaa4142a653f32).

HARD DEPENDENCY: task-9aca4b0524a648f1841237b40d4e345b (Security lane harness and declared-boundary roster) must be DONE — this slice consumes its harness and claims its `transport` axis tag. Re-measure the harness on disk before planning.

MEASURED BOUNDARY SUBSET at HEAD abc3dcf, listed with `grep -n '^export const'` not guessed. Every one of these is a declared layer constant carrying hostile-credential, stale-authority, replay, and race exposure:
- adapters/ide-contract/src/index.ts:26,29 — IDE_ADAPTER_LAYER, IDE_ADAPTER_LAYERS
- packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.ts:13 — CONTROL_ROOM_TRANSPORT_LAYER
- apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-contract.ts:16 — AFFORDANCE_SURFACE_LAYER
- apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream-observation.ts:14 — EVENT_STREAM_LAYER
- apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-guards.ts:13 — CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER_LAYER
- apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.ts:41 — DAEMON_ENTRY_LAYER
- apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority-contracts.ts:45 — SESSION_AUTHORITY_DAEMON_LAYERS
- packages/core/src/identity/authenticate-session.ts:16 — SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS
- packages/mcp/src/http/http-shutdown.ts:25 — HTTP_SHUTDOWN_LAYER
- packages/coordination/src/coordination-contracts.ts:25 — COORDINATION_LAYERS
- apps/control-room/src/timeline/timeline-contract.ts:38 — TIMELINE_REFUSAL_LAYERS
- apps/control-room/src/performance/effort-records.ts:34,35,37 — EFFORT_ADMISSION_LAYER, EFFORT_COLLECTOR_LAYER, EFFORT_LAYERS

Deliverable: hostile schedules against each of the above — forged/absent/expired credentials, stale authority presented after rotation, command replay, and a concurrent race at each admission point — each case asserting the exact stable reason code AND which layer answered.

NOT in scope: integrity/codec/approval boundaries, durable store faults, runtime/provider faults, scheduler/activation authority, closing the completeness ratchet, corpus bytes, or anything under tests/fault/**.

Owned paths: tests/security/transport-boundaries.security.ts (plus at most one sibling file if the 400-line split applies).

Verification: `pnpm test:security` — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code, and require it strictly above the pre-task baseline.
definitionOfDone: Every constant in the transport subset above has at least one BEFORE, one AFTER and one RACE case; the sweep asserts a positive case count per constant, so a schedule that silently generates zero cases for a boundary reddens instead of passing.

Every refusal assertion pins the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer constant — never merely that the operation did not succeed. Where two layers can refuse the same input, the fixture is valid at the earlier layer so the intended one answers.
No hostile case ever produces a success: a test asserts that across the whole file no case yields an admitted command, an issued grant, or a truth class above UNKNOWN.
Each race case is BOUNDED and terminates — the failure mode being guarded against is a hang, and a hanging test reports no verdict rather than a red one.

A mutation that removes one admission guard from a covered production boundary turns a NAMED test in this file red; the drill names which test and confirms the red lands on the intended assertion, not on an unrelated crash.

`pnpm test:security` runs with its exit code captured separately and prints a Test Files/Tests count line strictly above the pre-task baseline; the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta intersected with the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Consume the roster's `transport` axis tag as the definitive subset. Do not add, drop or re-tag a boundary here — the roster owns the partition, and an edit here silently creates an overlap or a gap with a sibling slice.
Drive the real production surfaces. A mock transport standing in for a real admission boundary proves the mock, not the boundary; test doubles are permitted only for the hostile input side.
Fail closed: an unobservable or refused transport interaction stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec. Do not touch tests/fault/**.

RESOLVE THE ONE BOUNDARY THAT MAY NOT BE REACHABLE, before writing 45 cases around it. `COORDINATION_LAYERS` is transport-tagged, but the coordination surface has NO production caller: `createCoordinationAdapter` is reachable only from its own test, and task-d17bb228 (which would have wired a command kind) is BLOCKED pending a human descope decision — the `RuntimeCommandKind` union is closed and expansion is ruled out for M5.
Measure it yourself, then choose ONE and say which in the file:
(a) COVER IT AT ITS OWN LAYER. The adapter, session authority and recipient registry are real and callable in-process. Hostile coverage of `send`/`acknowledge` against `createCoordinationAdapter` directly is honest transport coverage of that boundary's refusal semantics, even though no command kind routes to it today. This is the expected answer and keeps the axis complete.
(b) If the boundary genuinely cannot be exercised without the absent wire, say so explicitly in the file and in the completion, and DO NOT fabricate coverage. An UNKNOWN row that certifies nothing is better than a case driving a surface that cannot refuse.
What you must NOT do is quietly skip it: the ratchet task (task-3b1cbdf9) will later assert every roster entry resolves to a real before/after/race case, so a silent omission surfaces there as a late red with no owner. Decide now and record the decision.
implementationPlan.note:
COORDINATION_LAYERS DECISION: option (a) — COVER IT AT ITS OWN LAYER. Recorded here and to be restated in the file header.

Re-measurement corrected the plan on one point. The plan named `createCoordinationAdapter` as the surface to drive; that symbol does NOT exist in packages/coordination. `grep -rn createCoordinationAdapter --include=*.ts .` finds it only at apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.ts, referenced solely by its own test — the plan's "no production caller" claim is accurate, but the symbol lives in the DAEMON, not in the package that declares COORDINATION_LAYERS.

The right surface is `createCoordinationService`, and it is strictly better for this purpose:
- COORDINATION_LAYERS is declared in packages/coordination/src/coordination-contracts.ts, and createCoordinationService is that same package's own service — so driving it is coverage of the boundary AT ITS OWN LAYER in the literal sense, not via a daemon wrapper.
- It is exported from the package index (`export { createCoordinationService } from "./coordination-service.js"`), so it is a real public seam and not test-only reach.
- Its refusals are `CoordinationRefused { code, detail, layer, outcome: "REFUSED" }` where `layer` is a member of COORDINATION_LAYERS — exactly the shape assertRefusedWith reads, with no projection needed.
- Its guard chain is real production admission: clock -> authenticate (AUTHENTICATION) -> session ownership (AUTHENTICATION) -> capability (CAPABILITY) -> address/registry (ADDRESS) -> effect binding (ADDRESS) -> correlation (CORRELATION) -> decode (DECODE). Four distinct layers are reachable with hostile input alone, before the mailbox is ever consulted.

`CoordinationDependencies` is `{ authenticate, mailbox, now, resolveEffectBinding, resolveRecipient }`. The three port functions are the HOSTILE INPUT side, so doubles there are permitted by the task rail. The mailbox is downstream of admission and will be supplied as a stub that THROWS if touched — which does double duty: it is not a mock standing in for the admission boundary, and a case reaching it fails loudly instead of silently passing, proving admission refused before any store contact.

So the axis stays complete with no fabricated coverage and no UNKNOWN row. Option (b) is not needed.

The parse will itself assert it found exactly 15, so a regex that silently matches zero reddens instead of passing.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 1 — the BEFORE and AFTER arms across all 15 boundaries. Create `tests/security/transport-boundaries.security.ts` (the lane runs `**/*.security.ts`). Per boundary: at least one BEFORE case (hostile input arriving before the boundary has admitted anything — forged, absent, malformed or expired credentials; a malformed envelope; an oversized payload) and one AFTER case (authority presented after it should no longer be honoured — stale credential after rotation, revoked recipient, replayed command, closed or shut-down transport).
Every refusal goes through `assertRefusedWith(actual, {code, layer})` — both required, and the helper rejects a code-only call at compile time and at runtime. Take each expected layer from the boundary's OWN declared constant, not from a string literal you type: the point of the roster is that these constants are the vocabulary.
BUILD EACH FIXTURE VALID AT THE EARLIER LAYERS. Several of these boundaries sit behind another — an HTTP listener guard refuses before an affordance surface ever sees a request, and a transport-level malformed frame refuses before any session check. A fixture that is invalid at the earlier layer is answered there, and the assertion silently stops testing its subject. Where two layers can answer, say in a comment which one you arranged to answer and why.
ASSERT A POSITIVE CASE COUNT PER BOUNDARY, and assert the swept boundary set equals the roster's 15 transport entries in BOTH directions — a boundary that generated zero cases must redden rather than pass, and a case for a boundary outside this axis must redden too.
SPLIT IF NEEDED: 15 boundaries x 3 arms is 45+ cases. If a file would exceed 400 physical lines by `grep -c ''`, split into at most three `*.security.ts` files under tests/security/, keeping the roster-set assertion in ONE of them so the completeness check has a single home.
implementationPlan.note:
BEFORE and AFTER arms landed for all 15 roster transport boundaries, plus the roster-set completeness assertion.

EVERY EXPECTED LAYER IS READ OFF THE BOUNDARY'S OWN CONSTANT via layerOf(DECLARED, name), which throws if the constant stops declaring that member. No expected layer is a typed literal.

FIXTURES BUILT VALID AT THE EARLIER LAYERS, commented per boundary:
- IDE_ADAPTER_LAYER takes only UNRECOGNISED statuses (the contract's own arm); IDE_ADAPTER_LAYERS takes only RECOGNISED ones so the declared PORT answers instead.
- EFFORT_COLLECTOR fixtures are well-formed observations that already passed admission; a malformed one would be answered by EFFORT_ADMISSION_LAYER and the assertion would detach.
- TIMELINE PAGING fixtures carry a valid maxRows, because INPUT answers first.
- CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER order is Host, then Origin, then CSRF; each fixture is valid at every check ahead of the one it targets.
- COORDINATION send decodes, then authenticates, then resolves the address: the DECODE case smuggles a forbidden field, the AUTHENTICATION case presents a valid envelope with an UNFROZEN binding, the ADDRESS case presents a valid frozen binding with an unknown recipient.

BOUNDARY SET ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a case claiming a constant the roster does not tag transport reddens, and a roster entry with no case reddens naming the constant.

ONE DEVIATION FROM THE HARNESS CONTRACT, disclosed: DAEMON_INGRESS_LAYER spells its answering layer `refusedBy`, which readRefusal does not accept. decodeCompletion renames the FIELD only; both values still come from production and assertRefusedWith still compares code AND layer. The harness was NOT edited.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED WHILE WIRING: probeAfter(bound, effect, probe) puts the SECOND thunk in `.probe`, not `.effect`. Nine AFTER cases read the wrong leg and were asserting against the benign first result; six of them failed loudly, three passed only because both legs were hostile. All nine now read `.probe`.

`npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts transport-boundaries` -> EXIT=0, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 51 passed (51)`.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 2 — the RACE arm, which is the one most likely to be written unsoundly. Per boundary, one concurrent case through `probeRacing`, driving two operations that contend at the admission point: two sends claiming one recipient, a renew racing a revoke, a shutdown racing an in-flight request, an admission racing its own expiry.
EVERY RACE MUST BE BOUNDED AND MUST TERMINATE. The harness exposes `HostileBound` and `MAX_BOUND_MS = 2_147_483_647` — note that constant is 2**31-1, the `setTimeout` clamp boundary, so a bound at or above it clamps to 1ms and a case that meant "wait effectively forever" would instead race nothing. Pick bounds far below it and say why in a comment. The failure mode being guarded against is a hang, and a hanging test reports NO verdict rather than a red one — in a lane running `fileParallelism: false`, one hang stalls everything after it.
ASSERT THE RACE'S OUTCOME SHAPE, not merely that it completed: exactly one side is admitted and the other carries a stable code and layer, or both refuse — never two admissions. `RaceOutcome`/`LegOutcome` carry each side's result, so assert per-side rather than on an aggregate that could hide a double-admit.
AND ASSERT NON-DETERMINISM IS NOT REQUIRED: the test must pass whichever side wins. A race case that only passes when a particular leg wins is a flake that will be "fixed" by someone pinning the order, which destroys the property being tested.
FINALLY, ACROSS THE WHOLE SLICE: assert no hostile case — before, after or race — ever yields an admitted command, an issued grant, or a truth class above UNKNOWN. One assertion over the collected outcomes, not per case, so a newly added case cannot escape it.
implementationPlan.note:
RACE arm: 15 cases, one per roster transport boundary, all through `probeRacing`.

BOUNDED AND TERMINATING. Every race shares `BOUND = { label: "transport-boundary", timeoutMs: 2_000 }`. The comment on it states why 2s and not something larger: MAX_BOUND_MS is 2**31-1, the setTimeout clamp boundary, so a bound at or above it clamps to 1ms and would race nothing — this is six orders of magnitude below it. Whole file runs in 1.12s wall clock, so nothing is anywhere near the bound; a hang would report NO verdict rather than a red one, and in a `fileParallelism: false` lane it would stall every file after it.

ASSERTED PER SIDE, NEVER ON AN AGGREGATE. `assertSide(outcome.left, expected.left)` and `assertSide(outcome.right, expected.right)`, each going through `assertRefusedWith` with both code and layer. An aggregate assertion is exactly what could hide a double-admit.

ORDER-INDEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION. `left`/`right` are LEG POSITIONS, not settle order; `firstSettled` is never read by any assertion. A case that only passed when a particular leg won would be a flake, and the standard "fix" — pinning the order — destroys the property.

WHY ZERO ADMISSIONS RATHER THAN "EXACTLY ONE". Both legs of every race here are hostile, so a single admission is already the defect. The plan's general shape (one admitted, one refused) does not arise in this slice, and the stronger form is what is asserted.

WHOLE-SLICE INVARIANT, AND THE VACUITY I HAD TO REMOVE. First cut recorded `admitted: false` on every case because a refusal had been asserted — true by construction, so the invariant could never redden and was worse than no invariant at all. It now DERIVES admission from the value production returned, via `isAdmitted`, reading the boundaries' own positive vocabularies: `ok: true` (listener, daemon entry), `delivered: true` (client transport), `known: true` (effort, event-stream seam), and an `outcome` that is neither REFUSED nor UNKNOWN (ide adapter, timeline, affordance, coordination, import). A non-object counts as an admission, since every refusal on this axis is structured. Outcomes are recorded BEFORE the assertions run, so an admission reaches the invariant even when the case's own assertion fails first. Each race contributes TWO records, one per side, and a separate assertion pins `RECORDED.length === cases + races` so a dropped leg reddens instead of passing on the half it kept.

HONEST LIMIT, recorded rather than papered over: the affordance surface and the coordination service are SYNCHRONOUS, so their two legs are dispatched concurrently by the driver but cannot interleave mid-call. The property those two races establish is that concurrent dispatch at one admission point yields no admission on either side — not that a preemption window was exercised.

`npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts transport-boundaries` -> EXIT=0, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 51 passed (51)`.

implementationPlan.description:
CLEANUP AND ISOLATION — small but load-bearing in this lane. Every case that touches the filesystem takes its root from `hostileRoot(label)` or runs inside `withHostileRoot`, and the file registers `cleanupHostileRoots()` so every root is removed on every exit path INCLUDING a thrown or timed-out case. The lane runs `fileParallelism: false` and `isolate: true`, so a leaked root or a held handle stalls or poisons everything scheduled after it.
Close every resource a case opens — listeners, sockets, store handles, child processes — in a `finally`, not at the end of the happy path. A hostile case is precisely the one that leaves the throw path taken.
Do NOT touch `tests/fault/**`: it has other owners (tests/fault/disaster-restore/** belongs to task-0c89476b) and this slice is `tests/security/**` only. Do not modify `hostile-harness.ts` or `boundary-roster.security.ts` — both are committed deliverables of task-9aca4b05, and the roster in particular is the partition every sibling slice reads. If the harness genuinely lacks something this slice needs, report blocked rather than editing it; five slices share it and a local change would diverge them.
implementationPlan.note:
CLEANUP AND ISOLATION verified by measurement, not by reading the code.

FILESYSTEM. Exactly three cases touch disk — the AFFORDANCE_SURFACE_LAYER before/after/race trio — and all three go through `withHostileRoot(label, ...)`, which removes its root in a `finally` on every exit path including a throw. `transport-boundaries.security.ts` additionally registers `cleanupHostileRoots()` in `afterAll` as the belt-and-braces sweep.

MEASURED: `node -e "os.tmpdir()"` -> C:\Users\Yaron\AppData\Local\Temp; `ls -d $TMPDIR/moe-hostile-*` after a full green run -> count=0. Zero leaked roots. (Checking /tmp would have been the wrong probe here: MSYS maps /tmp to D:\tmp, which is not where Node creates them.)

RESOURCE HANDLES. `withPoisonedSurface` opens a real SqliteEventStore and closes it in a `finally`, so the store closes on the THROW path — which is precisely the path a hostile case takes. A held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker outright, and this lane runs `fileParallelism: false` with `isolate: true`, so one held handle would stall or poison everything scheduled after it. No case opens a listener, socket or child process; the daemon-entry cases refuse before any socket is bound, and the client-transport cases use an injected fetch that never opens one.

SHARED ARTIFACTS UNTOUCHED, measured with `git status --porcelain`:
  tests/security/hostile-harness.ts        -> no output (untouched)
  tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts -> no output (untouched)
  tests/fault/                              -> no output (untouched)
The DAEMON_INGRESS_LAYER field-name mismatch (`refusedBy` vs the harness's `layer`/`reasonLayer`) was the one place the harness fell short. I did NOT edit it — five slices share it. The case renames the field on its own side while both values still come from production and assertRefusedWith still compares code AND layer.

My three files are the only paths I have written: transport-boundaries.security.ts, transport-hostile-cases.ts, transport-hostile-fixtures.ts.

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS — prove the coverage is bound to real boundaries. Run each alone, revert before the next. (1) Remove one admission guard from a covered production boundary — for example the credential check behind `CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER_LAYER` or `AFFORDANCE_SURFACE_LAYER` — and confirm a NAMED case in this file reddens. Record which; a drill that reddens "the suite" proves less than one that names its test. (2) Change one boundary's declared layer constant and confirm the corresponding `assertRefusedWith` reddens on the LAYER mismatch specifically, not the code — the helper reports them separately, so check which message you got. (3) Delete one boundary's cases entirely and confirm the roster-set assertion from step 3 reddens naming that constant — proving the completeness check reads the roster rather than a hand-kept list. (4) Make one race case admit BOTH sides and confirm the per-side assertion reddens — proving the race asserts its outcome shape rather than merely that it finished.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Confirm each red lands on the INTENDED assertion, not an unrelated crash or a timeout. Restore with `git checkout -- <the one drilled file>` (never by hand — a hand restore goes ambiguous) and verify `git status --short` shows it clean before the next; drill 1 edits a PRODUCTION file in a shared worktree, so leaving it on disk risks a foreign completion hook committing it.

2) A FIXTURE ANSWERED BY THE WRONG LAYER. Several transport boundaries sit behind another — a listener guard refuses before an affordance surface sees the request.
